en: Run the portfolio and start every project with a charter and a clear go
Score proposals, sign charters and pass the gates before every start
every proposal is scored 1 to 5 on six weighted criteria, ranked and checked against your cut-off, so the monthly portfolio meeting starts from a ranked list
Business case with value and payback
investment, yearly benefit, years and discount rate give the net present value, the payback in months and a verdict against your payback limit
every project has a charter with purpose, objective and success measure, and a charter that waits too long for its sponsor shows as overdue to sign
Stage gate checks before a start
charter, scope, budget, team, risks and plan are six gates per project, each with a reviewer, evidence and a due date that warns before it is missed
RACI check for exactly one accountable
each activity is checked for one person responsible and exactly one accountable, and projects with rows to fix are flagged in the register
influence and interest give the engagement quadrant, and a sceptic with high influence is marked to win over first
Go and no-go decision log with review dates
every decision for a proposal or project keeps its readiness, conditions and review date, and a conditional go that is not reviewed on time turns overdue
amounts requested and approved, partly approved and declined requests and missing budget codes are separated so the finance partner knows what to open
the project days your team can give in a quarter are set against committed days and the effort of the proposals you would approve
each project is rated 1 to 5 against the six strategic objectives, so an objective that no project serves shows up at once
Project price from effort and margin
days by role at your own cost rates, vendors, contingency and margin give the cost, the price and how it compares with your charge rates
Quarterly budget with planned against actual
planned and actual spend of every project each quarter are compared with your amber and red limits

Purpose: {col:charters.purpose}. Objective: {col:charters.objective}. We will know the project has succeeded when this holds: {col:charters.success}.
The approved budget is {col:charters.budget}. The project starts on {col:charters.start} and its baseline end is {col:charters.end}.

The charter was drafted on {col:charters.drafted_on}. Its state is: {col:charters.state}. Signing it gives the project manager the authority to use the budget and to ask the team and the client for time and decisions.

The investment is {col:cases.investment}. The expected benefit is {col:cases.benefit_year} each year for {col:cases.years} years, discounted at {col:cases.rate}.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the score a proposal needs, the days a proposal may wait, the payback you accept and your warning days.
Fill Portfolio Register with every project: client, sponsor, manager, dates, budget, status, stage, priority, health and progress. Days late and the schedule state fill in.

Keep one charter per project on Project Charters and record the date it was signed. A charter that waits too long turns overdue to sign.

Record funding requests on Funding Approvals, staffing needs on Staffing Requests, and the planned and actual spend of each quarter on Quarterly Budget.
Rate each project against the six objectives on Strategy Alignment and write the monthly decision for each project on Portfolio Review Log.
Use the 14 calculators for business case value, priority score, project price, contingency, estimates, team size, scope change, readiness, cost of delay, break-even, capacity, funding and win rate.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: days to accept, the test exit level, fix targets by severity, health weights and colours, warranty warning and benefit limits.

Fill Projects with each project: client, contact, terms, manager, sponsor, dates, budget, spent, percent done, high risks, open issues and the client rating. Health and quality figures fill in from the other sheets.

List every deliverable and milestone on Deliverables and the criteria the client checks on Acceptance Criteria. Log each submission and decision on Acceptance Log; days to decide and late checks fill in.
Record test cycles on Test Cycles and key cases on Test Cases. Each failed case should have a defect on Defect Log; the check shows a failure without a defect.
Log defects with severity, finder, assignee and dates. Age, days to close, the fix target and the state fill in. Add the cause, fix hours and prevention action on Root Causes.
Enter review scores on Quality Reviews and effort, rework, review and prevention hours per month on Quality by Month. The rework share and defects found and closed fill in.

List each payment milestone on Payment Milestones with its deliverable, invoice number and dates. The due date comes from the client terms and the check warns of an invoice to send or an overdue payment.
Plan the handover on Handover Items and Support Transition, and the closing work on Closure Tasks. Overdue, blocked and ready states fill in by themselves.

Set each benefit on Benefits Register and enter the actual and planned value every month on Benefits Tracking. Record the post-project review on Post-Project Reviews and the signed proof on Acceptance Certificates.
Track each warranty on Warranty Periods: days left, the share of the period used and a warning before it ends.

Use the 14 calculators for defect density, removal efficiency, exit criteria, rework cost, acceptance and payment dates, milestone invoices, late payment interest, warranty, benefits, payback, health, handover and satisfaction.
